payload.body: Spectral-median (median frequency) is the full-spectrum energy-quantile summary that reports the frequency f_med at which half of the total spectral energy lies below and half above. Parameters: (1) the per-bin energy vector E = {E_i} over the full analyzed spectrum [f0, f_max), (2) the energy-weighted cumulative distribution C(f) = (sum of E_i for bins at frequency <= f) / (sum of all E_i), (3) the target quantile q, which the median fixes at q = 0.5; the reported value is the smallest frequency f such that C(f) >= q. It is a member of the same quantile family as spectral-rolloff, which fixes q at the 85% energy level: the median is the 50% level of that family and does not depend on a chosen high-level contour. It reads the full per-bin energy vector and carries no [f_low, f_high) band bounds, so it is a full-side summary rather than a band-local one. Persists as a standard energy-quantile summary in audio analysis, computed on the per-bin energy vector in MIR toolkits and reported in sound-description documentation. [formal: mediana spectri | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Electroglottography (EGG) is a non-invasive technique that measures glottal vocal-fold contact over time by passing a small alternating current through the vocal folds and recording the voltage across them. Because the glottal contact area modulates the electrical impedance of the vocal folds — high impedance when the glottis is open (air gap), low impedance when the folds are in contact — the peak-to-peak amplitude of the voltage is inversely related to glottal contact area, and its demodulated envelope, the electroglottogram (EGG waveform), tracks the open/close cycle of the glottis. Parameters: (1) excitation current — a small AC current kept below the safety threshold (typically ~0.5 mA peak at ~2.5 kHz); (2) electrode placement — two submental/neck electrodes completing the current path through the larynx; (3) demodulation — per-cycle peak-to-peak voltage measurement producing a continuous signal; (4) output — the electroglottogram, a time series whose amplitude is inversely proportional to glottal contact area. Persistence mechanism: standardized EGG transducers and laryngeal analysis systems (Kay PENTAGRAM, the laryngograph), documented in clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment; the waveform persists as a measured time series of glottal contact. Because the glottal contact area modulates the electrical impedance of the vocal folds — high impedance when the glottis is open (air gap), low impedance when the folds are in contact — the peak-to-peak amplitude of the voltage is inversely related to glottal contact area, and its demodulated envelope, the electroglottogram (EGG waveform), tracks the open/close cycle of the glottis. Parameters: (1) excitation current — a small AC current kept below the safety threshold (typically ~0.5 mA peak at ~2.5 kHz); (2) electrode placement — two submental/neck electrodes completing the current path through the larynx; (3) demodulation — per-cycle peak-to-peak voltage measurement producing a continuous signal; (4) output — the electroglottogram, a time series whose amplitude is inversely proportional to glottal contact area. Persistence mechanism: standardized EGG transducers and laryngeal analysis systems (Kay PENTAGRAM, the laryngograph), documented in clinical laryngology and voice-disorder assessment; the waveform persists as a measured time series of glottal contact. EGG requires a dedicated transducer and is not part of standard speech-processing.
